items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: And that was after I had finished with Charlie Ventura’s group.

ctx.x: Did they have any sense that you used to be in the middle of what was swinging popular music? Did they realize that?

Oh I think so, especially in the days when I got to stay home. See I spent an awful lot of time on the road. And so I started to stay home. I had a good Dixieland career down in Nick’s in Greenwich Village when it was the place for Dixieland. And actually that was the best steady jazz job in New York at the time. And so I played there for three or four years. And that was after I had finished with Charlie Ventura’s group. And I played there for about three or four years.
